observation_kinds.definition: The page or a page-level container visibly exceeds its intended viewport.
A child surface, card, label, or media item is visibly cut off or clipped.
A rendered module or heading is visible without the supporting content it promises.
A later visible module repeats information or media already presented without adding visible information.
Visible controls and identity or content surfaces have insufficient separation.
A visible word or lockup breaks at an awkward internal point or isolates a character.
Two visible modules perform substantially the same role in close succession.
Visible presentation makes side-by-side product comparison materially harder.
The supplied profiles visibly use meaningfully different structural presentation.
A visible condition that cannot be assigned safely to a more specific observation kind.

responsibility_ontology.use_when: Trusted provenance shows the condition arises from structural presenter composition, information hierarchy, navigation/grid/PDP relationships, or responsive transformation inherent to an architecture family.
responsibility_ontology.do_not_use_when: An architecture profile merely exists, or the condition is primarily a local arrangement, token constraint, absent content, or invalid data.

responsibility_ontology.use_when: The selected architecture is valid but generated modules are locally ordered, grouped, repeated, spaced, or left visibly empty without graceful fallback.
responsibility_ontology.do_not_use_when: The structural presenter itself creates the behavior, or one visual-system value is the primary cause.

responsibility_ontology.use_when: Structure is sound and typography scale, line-height, width, spacing, or breakpoint constraints primarily cause the visible condition.
responsibility_ontology.do_not_use_when: Changing a token would mask a structural hierarchy or presenter-composition defect.

responsibility_ontology.use_when: The design system handles the input correctly and merchant-supplied content is absent, excessive, low-quality, or inappropriate.
responsibility_ontology.do_not_use_when: Calinium knowingly renders an empty dependent module instead of suppressing or degrading it gracefully.

responsibility_ontology.use_when: Trusted context proves structured resource data is invalid, incomplete, or unavailable.
responsibility_ontology.do_not_use_when: The evidence establishes only aesthetic preference or ordinary merchant-content absence.

responsibility_ontology.use_when: Screenshots and trusted context cannot establish ownership reliably.
responsibility_ontology.do_not_use_when: A stricter boundary above is directly supported by trusted provenance.

dimension_rules.primary_when: The dominant visible issue is attention order among multiple surfaces.
dimension_rules.not_primary_when: A more specific typography, navigation, product-discovery, PDP, mobile, or composition rule applies.

dimension_rules.primary_when: Spacing cadence itself is the visible problem and no missing, duplicated, or miscomposed module explains it.
dimension_rules.not_primary_when: Blank space is downstream of an empty module or structural composition.

dimension_rules.primary_when: Text hierarchy, measure, wrapping, or legibility is the dominant visible condition.
dimension_rules.not_primary_when: Typography is merely affected by page overflow or header structure.

dimension_rules.primary_when: Media scale or sequencing itself creates the dominant visual consequence.
dimension_rules.not_primary_when: Repeated media is primarily an information-duplication issue.

dimension_rules.primary_when: Local module arrangement, repetition, grouping, or cross-surface relationship is the dominant condition.
dimension_rules.not_primary_when: A route-purpose dimension or page-level responsive failure is more specific.

dimension_rules.primary_when: Collection or product-browsing comprehension, comparison, or discovery is directly impaired.
dimension_rules.not_primary_when: A generic spacing or polish label only describes a downstream effect.

dimension_rules.primary_when: Product-page explanation, comparison, support, or purchase communication is directly affected.
dimension_rules.not_primary_when: The condition is a generic typography defect shared outside the PDP.

dimension_rules.primary_when: Header identity, navigation, search, or utility controls are directly crowded or unclear.
dimension_rules.not_primary_when: The issue is page-wide responsive containment outside the header.

dimension_rules.primary_when: Viewport containment or structural mobile transformation is the root visible condition.
dimension_rules.not_primary_when: A child truncation is only a symptom of an already identified page-level overflow.

dimension_rules.primary_when: Approved Design DNA is available and visible execution conflicts with it.
dimension_rules.not_primary_when: Design DNA is unavailable or only general aesthetic preference is visible.

dimension_rules.primary_when: A visible refinement issue remains after every specific functional/design dimension is ruled out.
dimension_rules.not_primary_when: It is being used as a catch-all for typography, spacing, composition, or navigation.

dimension_rules.primary_when: The finding directly compares meaningful structural behavior between bound profiles.
dimension_rules.not_primary_when: A defect happens within one profile merely because it has an architecture identity.

recommendation_taxonomy.definition: Adjust the class of responsive transformation or containment behavior.
Omit or gracefully degrade a module whose required content is unavailable.
Clarify the relationship among identity, navigation, search, and utility controls.
Correct the class of text measure, wrapping, scale, or containment behavior.
Remove or consolidate redundant local surfaces or information.
Omit content that is inappropriate or unsupported while the rendering system is otherwise correct.
Adjust the class of visual or informational priority among visible surfaces.
Record a legitimate preference without creating an independent repair recommendation.
Preserve the observation for human classification because intervention class is not safely inferable.
